description.narrative:
European Partnership Foundation (EPF) in Armenia has submitted an application to Sida for support to the project "Civil Society Support for Ensuring Impact on Reforms". The proposed duration of the project is 24 months, and the estimated budget is 1 476 773 USD, which amount to approximately 13 500 000 SEK.
The overarching objective of the proposed project is to "support the civil society in Armenia through building its capacities and strategic positioning to address the needs of the post-revolutionary situation in the areas of Human Rights, Anti-Discrimination and Non-Violence, Anti-Corruption and Conflict of Interest, Environment, Urban Planning and Development".
EPF intends to reach the overall objective by providing support in three main ways: - Support to CSOs responding to the challenges of democratic reform via open door and invited grants. - Capacity building for CSOs. - Networking within the civil society and between the civil society and the government.
The project intend to provide open calls and specific invited grant proposals to altogether approximately 40 CSOs throughout Armenia. EPF will conduct trainings for grant recipients and other CSOs, organize study trips, support networking and platforms for dialogue among civil society organisations and between civil society and the government. The project further aims to ensure that the watchdog and whistle-blower functions of the civil society will not be compromised as a result of increased dialogue and collaboration between the civil society and the government, something which is considered a risk in Armenia as many representatives of the rather newly established parliament and the government, themselves comes from the civil society.

Organisationen EPF har ansökt till Sida om finansiering om totalt 13 500 000 SEK för projeketet "Civil Society Support for Ensuring Impact on Reforms" i Armenien under perioden 2020-2021.
Insatsen syftar till att stödja civilsamhället i Armenien med kapacitetsutveckling och för att strategiskt kunna svara upp till de behov som uppstått efter revolutionen inom områdena mänskliga rättigheter, anti-diskriminering och icke-våld, anti-korruption och intressekonflikt, miljö samt stadsplanering och utveckling.
Insatsens totala budget uppgår till 13,5 miljoner SEK, varav ca 7,3 miljoner SEK kommer att vidareförmedlas till lokala civilsamhällesorganisationer.

The goal of the contribution is to strengthen the capacity and effectiveness of the civil society sector in responding to crises and driving impactful change towards a more resilient, sustainable and technologically advanced society.
The goal will be achieved through the implementation of the following two objectives:
1. To support the development of CSOs internal capacities and work practices through strategic consultations and mainstream trainings;
2. To support CS sector development effectiveness through strategic retreats, rapid response grants scheme, advocacy and research to contribute to the impact of CSOs on reform.

The project significantly strengthened Armenias civil society sector, particularly in crisis response and societal transformation.
EPF delivered trainings on financial management, fundraising, strategic planning, communications, and human rights advocacy. Identified gaps among smaller CSOs led to the creation of a financial reporting compendium. EPF conducted individual consultations using Capacity Enhancement Tool (CET) to assess and improve organizational strategies. Individual assessments of CSOs revealed strong leadership but weak governance structures. EPF helped formulate development strategies to address these gaps. Integrated capacity-building efforts across donor-funded projects, reaching 60 sub-grantees to foster broader collaboration and network-building.
Awarded sub-grants to partners aimed at supporting reforms in different sectors, including digitalization, with some of the results presented here.
EPFs re-grantee partner, Law Development and Protection Foundation, in consultation with Police of Armenia, MPs, representatives of judiciary and women rights organisations developed policy recommendations to improve practice of appealing urgent intervention decisions on domestic violence cases, identified gaps in the legislative framework, and outlined proposals to address these gaps. The project has identified that the existing system in Armenia for preventing domestic violence and safeguarding victims is inadequate, owing to gaps in legislation and flawed enforcement practices. The legal framework restricts timely action in situations of immediate risk, as urgent barring orders can be issued only after violence has taken place, which falls short of international standards.
Disablity Rigths Agenda NGO developed guidebook on disability rights education in schools by shifting from a medical to a human rights perspective, which was approved by the Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sports to include in the textbooks at schools.
Rights Center NGO analysed legal framework related to mental health institutions and proposing legislative revisions to integrate anonymous whistleblowing mechanisms designed to protect individuals from violations. The main outcome of the project was the development of a comprehensive legislative draft package, which included amendments to the Law on Psychiatric Care and Services and the Constitutional Law on the Defender of Human Rights. The project also created procedures for submitting anonymous reports on violations, as well as for examining complaints related to the rights of persons with mental health problems.
Global to Local Armenia NGO addressed the issue of bullying at schools built on the Swedish Olweus Bullying Prevention Program which emphasizes non-violent communication and conflict resolution through developing two modules of the program. The new modules were officially presented at the annual Global Forum on Social Justice in Schools and piloted with 35-40 teachers.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
